question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The sudden resign of (a)/ the finance minister (b)/ shocked everyone (c)/ on the eve of the budget. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After an article and an adjective ("the sudden …"), a noun is required before "of". "Resign" is a verb; its noun form is "resignation". So "the sudden resign of" must be "the sudden resignation of".

◦ Corrected sentence: The sudden resignation of the finance minister shocked everyone on the eve of the budget.

 

• A useful test — if the word can be preceded by "the / a / his / sudden" and followed by "of", it must be a noun, not a verb.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the finance minister" is a proper noun phrase in which "finance" acts as a noun modifier.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "shocked everyone" is a proper predicate (verb + object) in the simple past.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "on the eve of the budget" is a proper prepositional phrase of time.

 

NOTE

 

• Verb–noun pairs often tested: resign–resignation, decide–decision, arrive–arrival, refuse–refusal, propose–proposal, deny–denial, announce–announcement.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Before the ambulance arrived, (a)/ the injured cyclist was (b)/ rushed to a nearby clinic (c)/ by several passer-by. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a compound noun made of a noun + a preposition / adverb / adjective, the plural "-s" is added to the main noun, not to the end of the compound. So "passer-by" becomes "passers-by".

◦ Corrected sentence: Before the ambulance arrived, the injured cyclist was rushed to a nearby clinic by several passers-by.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Before the ambulance arrived," is a proper adverbial clause of time in the simple past.

 

• Part (b) is correct — the singular verb "was" agrees with the singular subject "the injured cyclist".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "rushed to a nearby clinic" is a proper past participle phrase in the passive voice.

 

NOTE

 

• Compound plurals: mothers-in-law, commanders-in-chief, runners-up, lookers-on, courts-martial, attorneys-general. But when no main noun is present, the last word takes the "-s": break-ins, lay-offs, grown-ups, hand-me-downs.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

In less than six month, (a)/ the construction of the flyover (b)/ was completed despite (c)/ frequent rain and labour shortage. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A noun that follows a numeral greater than one must be in the plural. "Six month" must therefore be "six months".

◦ Corrected sentence: In less than six months, the construction of the flyover was completed despite frequent rain and labour shortage.

 

• The singular form is used only when the number and noun join to form a hyphenated adjective before another noun — a six-month course.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the construction of the flyover" is a proper singular subject, and "flyover" is a correct singular noun after "of the".

 

• Part (c) is correct — the singular verb "was completed" agrees with the singular subject "construction", and "despite" is used correctly.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "frequent rain and labour shortage" is a proper noun phrase, and "rain" is acceptable as an uncountable noun here.

 

NOTE

 

• six months but a six-month course; ten years but a ten-year-old boy; two miles but a two-mile walk.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Before leaving the station, (a)/ the passengers were asked to (b)/ collect their belonging (c)/ from the security counter. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Belongings" (personal possessions) is a noun that is always used in the plural form. The singular "belonging" is used only in the sense of "a sense of being accepted" (a sense of belonging) and it does not agree with the plural pronoun "their".

◦ Corrected sentence: Before leaving the station, the passengers were asked to collect their belongings from the security counter.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Before leaving the station," is a proper participial phrase (before + gerund).

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the passengers were asked to" agrees in number and correctly uses the passive with an infinitive.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "from the security counter" is a proper prepositional phrase of place.

 

NOTE

 

• Nouns used only in the plural: belongings, surroundings, savings, earnings, valuables, remains, clothes, goods, thanks, congratulations, regards, arms, outskirts, ashes.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Due to a fall in demand, (a)/ the factory has (b)/ been running at a loss (c)/ and has announced several lays-off. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a compound noun is formed from a verb + a particle (adverb / preposition) — lay-off, break-in, check-up, stand-by, drop-out — there is no main noun inside it, so the plural "-s" is added at the end: "lay-offs", not "lays-off".

◦ Corrected sentence: Due to a fall in demand, the factory has been running at a loss and has announced several lay-offs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Due to a fall in demand," is a proper introductory phrase giving the reason.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the factory has" is the correct auxiliary for a singular subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "been running at a loss" correctly completes the present perfect continuous.

 

NOTE

 

• break-ins, check-ups, drop-outs, follow-ups, stand-bys, take-offs take "-s" at the end, but passers-by, runners-up, sisters-in-law take it on the main noun.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The police searched (a)/ the entire premise (b)/ of the factory (c)/ but found nothing. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Premises" (a building together with its land) is a noun that is always plural in form. The singular "premise" means "a statement on which an argument is based", so it is wrong here. The correct phrase is "the entire premises".

◦ Corrected sentence: The police searched the entire premises of the factory but found nothing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The police searched" is properly formed, since "police" is a plural noun and the past tense verb needs no agreement.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "of the factory" is a proper prepositional phrase.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "but found nothing" is a proper coordinate verb phrase with the same subject.

 

NOTE

 

• Some nouns change meaning in the plural: premise → premises, custom → customs, arm → arms, spectacle → spectacles, manner → manners, letter → letters, ash → ashes.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The organisers distributed (a)/ three thousands posters (b)/ and six hundred pamphlets (c)/ across the city. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The words hundred, thousand, lakh, crore, million, dozen, score, pair do not take "-s" when they follow a definite number and a noun comes after them. So "three thousands posters" must be "three thousand posters".

◦ Corrected sentence: The organisers distributed three thousand posters and six hundred pamphlets across the city.

 

• The plural form is used only when the number is indefinite and "of" follows — thousands of posters, hundreds of people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The organisers distributed" is a proper subject and verb in the simple past.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "and six hundred pamphlets" correctly keeps "hundred" in the singular.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "across the city" is a proper prepositional phrase of place.

 

NOTE

 

• five dozen eggs but dozens of eggs; two hundred students but hundreds of students; three lakh rupees but lakhs of rupees.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The charity organises (a)/ free medical camps (b)/ in remote villages (c)/ for aged. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An adjective can act as a noun for a whole class of people only when it is preceded by "the" — the aged, the poor, the blind, the sick. The adjective "aged" cannot stand alone as a noun, so "for aged" must be "for the aged".

◦ Corrected sentence: The charity organises free medical camps in remote villages for the aged.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — the singular verb "organises" agrees with the singular subject "The charity".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "free medical camps" is a proper plural noun phrase used as the object.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "in remote villages" is a proper prepositional phrase of place.

 

NOTE

 

• the + adjective = plural noun and takes a plural verb: The poor are often ignored; The young are the future of the nation.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Many customers (a)/ buy smartphones (b)/ of these type (c)/ because they offer a long battery life. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A demonstrative adjective must agree in number with the noun that follows it. "Type / kind / sort" are singular, so they take this / that (this type of smartphone); for the plural, both the demonstrative and the noun become plural (these types of smartphones). "These type" mixes a plural demonstrative with a singular noun.

◦ Corrected sentence: Many customers buy smartphones of this type / these types because they offer a long battery life.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Many customers" is a proper plural subject with the quantifier "many".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "buy smartphones" is a proper plural verb phrase in the simple present.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "because they offer a long battery life" is a proper clause of reason, and "they" agrees with "smartphones".

 

NOTE

 

• this kind of book / these kinds of books; that sort of person / those sorts of people. Never write these kind, those sort or these type.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The new sport complex (a)/ built by the school (b)/ has facilities for (c)/ students of all classes. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Some nouns are used in the plural form even when they act as modifiers in a fixed compound: sports complex, savings account, customs officer, arms race, accounts department. The correct phrase is therefore "sports complex", not "sport complex".

◦ Corrected sentence: The new sports complex built by the school has facilities for students of all classes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "built by the school" is a proper past participle phrase qualifying "complex".

 

• Part (c) is correct — the singular verb "has" agrees with the singular subject "complex".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "students of all classes" is a proper noun phrase with "of".

 

NOTE

 

• sports car, sports day, sports shoes; savings bank, earnings report, arms dealer. Note that sport is used in a general sense (He plays every sport).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Every evening, (a)/ the retired colonel walks along the riverside (b)/ and goes for running (c)/ before the sun sets. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• With "go for", a noun must follow — go for a run, a walk, a swim, a drive. A gerund ("running") is not used after "go for". One may correctly say either "goes for a run" or "goes running".

◦ Corrected sentence: Every evening, the retired colonel walks along the riverside and goes for a run before the sun sets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Every evening," is a proper adverbial of time and needs no preposition.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the retired colonel walks along the riverside" is a proper subject and verb in the simple present, with a correct prepositional phrase of place.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "before the sun sets" is a proper clause of time in the simple present.

 

NOTE

 

• go for a walk, go for a swim, go for a ride, go for a drink (noun) but go walking, go swimming, go shopping (gerund without "for").

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The Chief Minister of Kerala (a)/ visit to the flood-hit (b)/ area has boosted (c)/ the morale of the people. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a title or a group of words ends in an "of + noun" phrase, the possessive 's is attached to the last word of the whole phrase (group genitive). So "The Chief Minister of Kerala" becomes "The Chief Minister of Kerala's" before the noun "visit".

◦ Corrected sentence: The Chief Minister of Kerala's visit to the flood-hit area has boosted the morale of the people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "visit to the flood-hit" is a proper noun with the preposition "to".

 

• Part (c) is correct — the singular verb "has boosted" agrees with the singular subject "visit".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "the morale of the people" is a proper noun phrase serving as the object.

 

NOTE

 

• Group genitive: the Prime Minister of India's speech, the Queen of England's crown, my sister-in-law's house, the King of Nepal's palace.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Before boarding the flight, (a)/ the tourists packed (b)/ their laptops and (c)/ camera's carefully. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The apostrophe + s shows possession; it is never used to form a plain plural. "Cameras" here is simply the plural of "camera", so "camera's" must be "cameras".

◦ Corrected sentence: Before boarding the flight, the tourists packed their laptops and cameras carefully.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Before boarding the flight," correctly uses "before" with a gerund.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the tourists packed" is a proper plural subject and verb in the simple past.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "their laptops and" is correct, since "their" agrees with the plural "tourists" and "laptops" is a proper plural.

 

NOTE

 

• The girl's are playing (wrong) → The girls are playing. Use the apostrophe only for possession: the girl's bag (one girl), the girls' bags (many girls).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Several passengers (a)/ complained at the airport (b)/ after the long flight (c)/ about their missing baggages. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Baggage" (like luggage, furniture, equipment and machinery) is an uncountable noun. It has no plural form, so "baggages" is wrong. The correct form is "baggage", or "pieces of baggage" when counting.

◦ Corrected sentence: Several passengers complained at the airport after the long flight about their missing baggage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Several passengers" is a proper plural subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "complained at the airport" is a proper verb phrase with a prepositional phrase of place.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "after the long flight" is a proper prepositional phrase of time.

 

NOTE

 

• Uncountable nouns: baggage, luggage, furniture, equipment, machinery, scenery, information, advice, knowledge, news, evidence, jewellery, homework. Count them with a piece of / an item of / an article of.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Scientists have identified (a)/ nearly forty new specieses (b)/ of frogs in (c)/ the Western Ghats. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Species" has the same form in the singular and the plural. The form "specieses" does not exist, so the correct phrase is "forty new species".

◦ Corrected sentence: Scientists have identified nearly forty new species of frogs in the Western Ghats.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Scientists have identified" is a proper plural subject with the present perfect.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "of frogs in" is a proper phrase with the correct prepositions.

 

• Part (d) is correct — the name of a mountain range takes "the", so "the Western Ghats" is right.

 

NOTE

 

• Nouns with the same singular and plural: species, series, sheep, deer, fish, offspring, aircraft, means, crossroads, salmon.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Most engineers agree that early maintenance (a)/ proves to be more economical (b)/ than replace (c)/ after a major breakdown. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a comparison, the two things compared must be of the same grammatical form. "Early maintenance" (a noun) is compared here with "replace" (a verb), which is faulty. After "than", the noun "replacement" is required.

◦ Corrected sentence: Most engineers agree that early maintenance proves to be more economical than replacement after a major breakdown.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Most engineers agree that early maintenance" is a proper main clause with a noun clause opener.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "proves to be more economical" correctly uses the comparative with "more".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "after a major breakdown" is a proper prepositional phrase of time.

 

NOTE

 

• Parallelism — compare noun with noun, gerund with gerund: Prevention is better than cure, Walking is healthier than driving.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Scientists explained (a)/ that the moon gravitational (b)/ pull is responsible (c)/ for the ocean tides. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The possessive case ('s) is used with nouns showing living beings, and also with the sun, moon, earth, nature and time. "The moon gravitational pull" lacks the possessive marker and must be "the moon's gravitational pull".

◦ Corrected sentence: Scientists explained that the moon's gravitational pull is responsible for the ocean tides.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Scientists explained" is a proper subject and verb in the simple past.

 

• Part (c) is correct — the singular verb "is responsible" agrees with the singular subject "pull".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "for the ocean tides" is a proper prepositional phrase with "responsible for".

 

NOTE

 

• the sun's rays, the earth's surface, nature's beauty, a day's work, a stone's throw — the possessive is used with celestial bodies, nature and time expressions.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

Our mentor shared many valuable knowledges (a)/ with the students (b)/ during the workshop. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Knowledge" is an uncountable noun and has no plural form, so "knowledges" is wrong. It is also not used with "many"; use "much" or "a great deal of".

◦ Corrected sentence: Our mentor shared much valuable knowledge with the students during the workshop.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "with the students" is a proper prepositional phrase after "shared".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "during the workshop." is a proper prepositional phrase of time.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "knowledges" in part (a) is incorrect.

 

NOTE

 

• Uncountable: knowledge, advice, information, news, furniture, luggage, equipment, evidence, progress, homework — use much / a little / some and not many / a few.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The engineers' report (a)/ on the bridge collapse (b)/ was submitted to the minister. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is grammatically correct. "The engineers' report" correctly shows plural possession — the apostrophe follows the plural "s" (the report of several engineers).

◦ Sentence as given: The engineers' report on the bridge collapse was submitted to the minister.

 

• "Bridge collapse" is a correct noun compound in which the first noun acts as a modifier and stays singular, and the singular verb "was submitted" agrees with the singular subject "report".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — the plural possessive "engineers'" is properly formed with the apostrophe after the "s".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "on the bridge collapse" is a proper prepositional phrase, and the noun modifier "bridge" needs no "-s".

 

• Part (c) is correct — the passive "was submitted to the minister" agrees with "report".

 

NOTE

 

• Do not over-correct: the girl's book (one girl) vs the girls' books (many girls). A noun used as an adjective stays singular — a shoe shop, a bridge collapse.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The scientist (a)/ had never doubted (b)/ his firm believe in (c)/ the power of experiments. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After the possessive "his" and the adjective "firm", a noun is required. "Believe" is a verb; the noun is "belief". So "his firm believe in" must be "his firm belief in".

◦ Corrected sentence: The scientist had never doubted his firm belief in the power of experiments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The scientist" is a proper singular subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "had never doubted" correctly uses the past perfect with "never".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "the power of experiments" is a proper noun phrase that completes the sense.

 

NOTE

 

• Noun forms that change spelling: believe–belief, prove–proof, lose–loss, live–life, speak–speech, choose–choice, grieve–grief, succeed–success.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The doctor warned (a)/ that the side affect (b)/ of the medicine (c)/ could be dangerous. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Effect" is the noun meaning "a result or consequence", while "affect" is normally a verb meaning "to influence". After "the side …", a noun is needed, so "side affect" must be "side effect".

◦ Corrected sentence: The doctor warned that the side effect of the medicine could be dangerous.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The doctor warned" is a proper subject and verb in the simple past.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "of the medicine" is a proper prepositional phrase after the noun.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "could be dangerous" correctly uses the modal with the adjective.

 

NOTE

 

• Effect (noun) = result; affect (verb) = influence — Pollution has a bad effect on health, Pollution affects health. Remember: Affect = Action; Effect = End result.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

He was determined (a)/ to win the election (b)/ by fair (c)/ or foul mean. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Means" (method or way) is a noun whose form does not change in the singular and plural. The singular "mean" is used only as an adjective (stingy) or in the mathematical sense (average), so "by fair or foul means" is the correct phrase.

◦ Corrected sentence: He was determined to win the election by fair or foul means.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "He was determined" is a proper subject and predicate adjective.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "to win the election" is a proper infinitive phrase after "determined".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "by fair" begins the correct phrase "by fair or foul means" and needs no change.

 

NOTE

 

• by all means, by no means, a means to an end, ways and means. Also, when "means" denotes wealth, it takes a plural verb — His means are limited.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The remarks he made (a)/ during the interview (b)/ were highly controversy (c)/ and hurt many people. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After the adverb "highly" and the verb "were", an adjective is required. "Controversy" is a noun; its adjective form is "controversial". So "were highly controversy" must be "were highly controversial".

◦ Corrected sentence: The remarks he made during the interview were highly controversial and hurt many people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The remarks he made" is a proper plural subject with a relative clause.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "during the interview" is a proper prepositional phrase of time.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "and hurt many people" is a proper coordinate verb phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• Noun–adjective pairs: controversy–controversial, danger–dangerous, courage–courageous, envy–envious, prosperity–prosperous, victory–victorious.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The trust (a)/ provides free stationary (b)/ to poor students (c)/ every year. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Stationery" (with -ery) is a noun meaning writing materials such as paper, pens and envelopes. "Stationary" (with -ary) is an adjective meaning "not moving". So "free stationary" must be "free stationery".

◦ Corrected sentence: The trust provides free stationery to poor students every year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The trust" is a proper singular subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "to poor students" is a proper prepositional phrase after "provides".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "every year" is a proper adverbial of frequency.

 

NOTE

 

• Memory aid: stationEry — EnvElopes / paper (a noun); stationAry — stAnding still (an adjective). Similarly principal / principle, complement / compliment, site / sight.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The dentist told him (a)/ that three of his (b)/ tooths needed (c)/ immediate extraction. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Tooth" is an irregular noun; its plural is formed by an internal vowel change — "teeth". The form "tooths" does not exist.

◦ Corrected sentence: The dentist told him that three of his teeth needed immediate extraction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The dentist told him" is a proper subject, verb and indirect object.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "that three of his" correctly begins the noun clause with a plural quantity.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "immediate extraction" is a proper noun phrase that completes the sense.

 

NOTE

 

• Irregular plurals: tooth–teeth, foot–feet, goose–geese, mouse–mice, louse–lice, man–men, woman–women, child–children, ox–oxen.
